preview_en:
Last season’s 2.Bundesliga champions Schalke look to make ground on Elversberg , who may have finished eight points behind the hosts last term but have made a stunning start to the new campaign.

Match News and Current Form

Schalke ended a 1203-day wait to score a top-flight goal on matchday three when they recorded their first win of the campaign against Union Berlin (D1, L1). That represents a stronger start than their last two top-flight seasons, both of which ended in relegation, as they now switch their attention to picking up three Bundesliga home points for the first time since April 2023. That seems like a realistic expectation as Schalke are currently enjoying their longest run of unbeaten home league games since 1992 (W11, D4), while they’ve lost just one of the last nine matches they hosted in the top flight (W3, D5).

Despite putting up a spirited fight, Elversberg saw their perfect four-game winning start to the competitive season ended with a 2-1 defeat against Bayern Munich in the last round. Now at risk of posting consecutive defeats for the first time since October, Elversberg will be leaning heavily on an attack which has scored in each of their last 12 games, which if they extend to 13 would represent a new club record. Following back-to-back away victories, the visitors' area for improvement is clearly at the back, as they’re currently enduring a negative club-record 16-game wait for a competitive away clean sheet.

Head-to-Head History

Schalke beat Elversberg home and away in last season’s 2.Bundesliga, but they have fallen to defeat in two of the last three home H2Hs (W1). Between any two promoted sides, the home side on the day won six of the last nine such Bundesliga games (W6, D1, L2).

Hot Stats and Streaks

Just one of Schalke’s last six league games saw both teams score.

Schalke have lost just two of their last 13 Bundesliga home games against promoted sides (W7, D4).

Elversberg have scored 3+ goals in three of their last four competitive away games.

Elversberg’s last ten games produced over 2.5 goals.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Schalke goalkeeper Loris Karius has made a pre-round Bundesliga-high 22 saves this season, with another league-high shot saving rate of 84% - he has also kept a clean sheet in three of his four career H2Hs against Elversberg. Trying to break down that wall will be Maurice Krattenmacher , who is now the first player ever for a promoted side to score three goals as a substitute in the opening three rounds of a Bundesliga season.

Bryan Lasme and Adrian Gantenbein are doubts for Schalke, while Elversberg’s Francis Onyeka is also doubtful with a knock.

Betting Analysis

A difficult game to call a result between two promoted sides could hint that both teams to score is an alternative route to value.

Author: Matthew Billon
